sources.title: Exploring the Nottoway River from Hercules Landing
sources.author: John Page Williams
sources.acquired_scope: Original state-published article opened normally in the web text reader; geographic and lower-river prose actually read. No linked photographs or maps were used as cartographic evidence.
sources.supports: The Nottoway runs from the Virginia Piedmont toward Southampton, joins the Blackwater just below the state line, and continues as the Chowan toward Albemarle Sound. Hercules Landing lies on the lower Nottoway south of the Courtland–Franklin area; the article describes this section as tidal fresh water.
sources.limits: Supporting prose corroborates the downstream name progression but does not identify every selected headwater reach, reservoir crossing or exact terminal. Its stated length is not substituted for retained model length. The article footer carries Virginia DWR copyright; no photos or article reproduction are distributed.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern opening and upper connector into the southern map overlap
correspondence.finding: The original geographical-subdivisions map on Bulletin 18 page 4 has readable latitude/longitude ticks and distinguishes continuous Inland Ice from the exposed coastal belts. The northern opening and its southward/southwestward connector occupy the mapped southwestern Inland Ice interior, well inland of the western coastal belt. That continuous interior setting extends south into the 62°30′N boundary region covered by the 2007 detailed sheet.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at bounded generalized regional/component scale
correspondence.limits: The page 4 overview establishes broad ice-interior correspondence only; it does not supply a river trace, subglacial hydrology, a local channel name or precise ice/basin boundaries. Its pixels were actually read; this is not an inference from a catalogue extent or general prose alone.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper mapped southern corridor and southwestward middle steps
correspondence.finding: South of the northern sheet boundary, the original graticule places the selected southwestward sequence across the continuous light-blue ice surface. Ice-surface contours continue across this middle corridor. Exposed western-margin terrain lies away from the selected course. No mapped river label or river-channel sequence corresponding to these interior steps is established.
correspondence.correspondence: bounded geographic setting read from original cartography
correspondence.limits: Ice and elevation contours are not surface or subglacial river traces.

correspondence.component_scope: Stepped middle descent and long near-southward approaches
correspondence.finding: The overlapping original middle and southern views cover the small southwestward steps, the long near-southward intervals and their approach to the southern ice margin. This selected corridor remains on mapped ice toward the Søndre Qipisaqqu Bræ setting. The map does not show a selected through-lake, reservoir or river confluence that would license a river-system name.
correspondence.correspondence: bounded geographic setting read from original cartography
correspondence.limits: The glacier label is local margin context and is not propagated upstream over the complete modeled mainstem. No present flow direction, glacier catchment boundary or contemporary ice extent is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Final southwestward approach, short turn and actual terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The original detailed pixels place the final approach at the southern ice-front/inner-fjord setting of Sermilik, west of the intervening bedrock peninsula and the separate Bredefjord corridor. The ending is at the narrow northeastern inner-head vicinity, rather than at the outer coastal mouth. The map distinguishes ice, exposed bedrock and fjord water here.
correspondence.correspondence: actual terminal setting read at generalized corridor scale
correspondence.limits: This is a historical map setting, not a surveyed mouth, present ice front or exact shoreline intersection. Sermilik and Søndre Qipisaqqu Bræ are not accepted names for the modeled river group.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening in the western Canatlán highlands
correspondence.finding: The retained short westward/northwestward opening corresponds to the small west-draining course on the western flank of Cerro Colorado in Canatlán. The municipal original shows this headwater approaching the San Dimas boundary, where the adjacent San Dimas original continues the southward valley. The Santiago drainage to the east and the more northerly Arroyo Quebrada Santa Rosa are distinct mapped courses.
correspondence.limits: The first modeled reach has no established hydronym in the inspected maps. Cerro Colorado is a terrain orientation label, not a river name. No precise source point is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Miravalles upper course and joining sector
correspondence.finding: The selected southward then southwestward course follows the valley directly labeled Miravalles on the San Dimas Relieve map. The state sheet supplies the Doce de Mayo and Río de Miravalles locality setting and the continuous southwestward joining course toward the trunk labeled Río Piaxtla. The adjacent Piedra Parada and other side-drainage approaches remain separate from the selected northern approach.
correspondence.limits: Río de Miravalles is also a locality inscription on the state sheet; the hydronym observation comes from the municipal Relieve map. No exact Miravalles/Piaxtla name-transition vertex or formal naming boundary is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Piaxtla canyon and Durango–Sinaloa continuation
correspondence.finding: The retained course continues west and southwest on the mapped Piaxtla through the Carboneras/General Rafael Buelna and Tayoltita setting, then follows the canyon across the Durango–Sinaloa boundary. The river is continuous into the San Ignacio municipal map; the more southerly Presidio course is a separate drainage.
correspondence.limits: Settlement names locate the corridor. They are not added as hydronyms, and no unselected side branches are added.

correspondence.component_scope: San Ignacio middle course and northern bend
correspondence.finding: The selected westward course crosses the San Ignacio setting on the stream labeled Río Piaxtla. The maps show the separate Río Verde approach from the north near Ajoya/El Platanar joining the Piaxtla corridor, followed by the west/northwest reach through the San Javier/Coacoyol sector and the pronounced bend back south. This full joining and bending corridor corresponds to the retained middle selection.
correspondence.limits: The Río Verde approach is contextual and is not a separately selected tributary feature. Exact confluence vertices are not adjudicated.

correspondence.component_scope: Coastal plain and actual terminal corridor
correspondence.finding: Below the northern bend the selected course turns southwest through the Piaxtla de Arriba/Piaxtla de Abajo and Duranguito–Dimas coastal-plain setting. The state original continues the same Río Piaxtla channel to the coast immediately north of Barras de Piaxtla. The Elota/Ceuta outlet to the northwest and Estero el Pozole farther southeast are separate coastal features, not substitutes for the selected terminal.
correspondence.limits: The receiving-water setting is the Pacific coast at southern Sinaloa. No exact present-day inlet, bank, shoreline intersection or surveyed mouth coordinate is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake and reservoir context across the full selected corridor
correspondence.finding: No major named lake or reservoir passage is depicted on the selected route in the inspected maps. Presa las Truchas, Presa Aurelio Benassini Vizcaíno (El Salto) and Presa Picachos are visibly on separate neighboring drainage settings. They are not assigned to this feature.
correspondence.limits: This is a statement about the inspected cartographic corridor, not a present-day inventory of every small impoundment or a claim about current regulation or flow.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward selection and eastern reservoir connector
correspondence.finding: The fine topographic map places the selected opening in the small streams and agricultural-drainage landscape northwest of El Refugio. It distinguishes the La Tabaquera-side hills and other local feeders from the larger Salado approach through Tala. The original La Vega zoning map shows the named eastern Salado connection into the reservoir, supplying bounded east-inlet correspondence. Initial exact name remains null.
correspondence.limits: The rural opening is mapped as several local/intermittent and engineered drainage elements, with historical/generalized differences in lake entry. This is corridor correspondence, not an exact assignment of one hydronym or proof of a continuously active modern channel at every modeled point.

correspondence.component_scope: La Vega reservoir and southern outlet
correspondence.finding: The selection continues through the La Vega impoundment and leaves its southern end by the dam/La Vega settlement. Northern Teuchitlán inflows, western Chapulimita/Cocolisco-side drainage and the southeastern Cuisillos–Salado approach remain distinguishable; none is automatically the selected opening.
correspondence.limits: The rural opening is mapped as several local/intermittent and engineered drainage elements, with historical/generalized differences in lake entry. This is corridor correspondence, not an exact assignment of one hydronym or proof of a continuously active modern channel at every modeled point.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Ameca valley
correspondence.finding: Downstream of La Vega, the route runs west/southwest through the irrigated valley toward Ameca, then northwest by San Nicolás, Jayamitla and the San Blasito/Jesús María boundary setting. The regional map labels the matching channel Ameca.
correspondence.limits: The rural opening is mapped as several local/intermittent and engineered drainage elements, with historical/generalized differences in lake entry. This is corridor correspondence, not an exact assignment of one hydronym or proof of a continuously active modern channel at every modeled point.

correspondence.component_scope: Boundary reach and major middle junctions
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the northwest-trending Ameca along the Jalisco–Nayarit boundary, past the Amatlán de Cañas/Tepuzhuacán sector, the Atenguillo junction, the broad northern bend and then the west/southwest course by El Ahuejote and Aguamilpa. The map separately labels the Los Reyes tributary entering this downstream sector.
correspondence.limits: The rural opening is mapped as several local/intermittent and engineered drainage elements, with historical/generalized differences in lake entry. This is corridor correspondence, not an exact assignment of one hydronym or proof of a continuously active modern channel at every modeled point.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower valley and transition to second feature
correspondence.finding: The Ameca turns southwest from Aguamilpa/El Colomo into the San José del Valle–San Vicente–Ixtapa lowland. Mascota approaches independently from the southeast and joins in the lower valley near the transition to the final feature.
correspondence.limits: The rural opening is mapped as several local/intermittent and engineered drainage elements, with historical/generalized differences in lake entry. This is corridor correspondence, not an exact assignment of one hydronym or proof of a continuously active modern channel at every modeled point.

correspondence.component_scope: Final lower Ameca and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The original state map carries the matching Ameca channel to the bay; it also distinguishes the southern Pitillal river and nearby coastal settlements. Regional primary prose independently identifies Bahía de Banderas as the Ameca receiving water.
correspondence.limits: Regional cartographic scale supports the estuary and bay identity, not exact modern mouth position or bank alignment.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward fork and Nottoway junction
correspondence.finding: South of Oliveville and Twin Bridges Road, the selected western opening follows the directly labeled North Fork Nottoway River corridor east toward its junction with the separately labeled Nottoway River. The continuing river turns south and southeast along the Nottoway–Lunenburg county-border setting toward Rubermont. The separately mapped western Nottoway approach and the northern Snail Creek approach are distinct from the selected opening.
correspondence.limits: This is corridor correspondence, not a precise junction or natural-source assignment.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Nottoway, reservoir and eastern continuation
correspondence.finding: The route continues southeast and then east along the Nottoway county-border corridor, receiving the Big Hounds Creek approach and reaching the Little Nottoway junction southwest of Blackstone. It passes through the mapped Nottoway Reservoir and its southeast outlet, then proceeds east and southeast along the Nottoway through the Dinwiddie–Brunswick boundary setting toward the Sussex–Greensville side.
correspondence.limits: Little Nottoway is the northern joining tributary, not the selected upstream branch. Nottoway Reservoir retains its mapped impoundment identity.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Nottoway and Sussex bend
correspondence.finding: The selected course follows the Nottoway eastward to the Interstate 95/US 301 corridor, then its conspicuous northward loop toward the Stony Creek joining setting. It continues east across the Sussex interior before turning south and southeast. The connected floodplain channel, route crossings and repeated Nottoway labels cover the whole selected middle corridor.
correspondence.limits: Stony Creek, nearby swamps and lesser branches remain junction context; no exhaustive tributary naming is attempted.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Nottoway through Southampton
correspondence.finding: The river descends through the Three Creek junction neighborhood and Southampton County, passes the Courtland/US 58 corridor west of Franklin, and continues southeast through the wooded lower Nottoway toward the state line. The Nottoway remains separately labeled from the Blackwater River approaching south from Franklin on the east. The original map shows their junction just below the Virginia–North Carolina boundary, followed by the Chowan. Virginia DWR prose independently states that the Nottoway and Blackwater join to form the Chowan.
correspondence.limits: The Blackwater approach is not selected. Supporting prose also describes the full downstream river, which is longer than the retained selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Chowan and Meherrin junction
correspondence.finding: Below the Nottoway–Blackwater junction the selected channel turns south, bends west and then south toward Winton. It is directly labeled Chowan River before receiving the separately labeled Meherrin River from the west. The first retained feature ends in this junction neighborhood, and the second continues on the same mapped Chowan channel.
correspondence.limits: No exact fragment seam is asserted to equal a hydronym boundary or tributary mouth point.

correspondence.component_scope: Winton and eastward Chowan
correspondence.finding: From immediately below the Meherrin joining neighborhood the selected route passes Winton and the US 13 crossing, turns southeast and then east along the Gates–Hertford boundary, and continues through the mapped Chowan bends by Rays Beach and Pettys Shore. Multiple direct Chowan River labels follow this full channel.
correspondence.limits: Meherrin and nearby creeks are independent tributaries and are not assigned the Chowan representative name.

correspondence.component_scope: Widening Chowan and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected southeastward lower section passes the western Wiccacon joining setting and continues into the wider Chowan opposite the Bennetts Creek side. It ends in the broad river near the Bennetts Creek–Catherine Creek junction neighborhood, above Holiday Island. The viewed original extends beyond the retained end, making clear that the Chowan continues downstream rather than terminating there.
correspondence.limits: Bennetts Creek and Catherine Creek are eastern joining waters, not the selected route. The selected endpoint is not Albemarle Sound, an ocean shoreline or the natural mouth of the Chowan.
